passage: Abstract: "record-wise CV often massively overestimates the prediction accuracy of the algorithms"; "the subject-wise method mirrors the clinically relevant use-case scenario of diagnosis in newly recruited subjects".
faulty: Record-wise 10-fold cross-validation: all 16 x 60 = 960 recordings are assigned to folds uniformly at random, each carrying its subject's disease label; a random forest (50 trees) scores each recording; the AUC of the pooled held-out scores is the statistic. Claim holds when AUC >= 0.70.
fixed: Subject-wise cross-validation: all recordings of a subject are in the same fold (leave-two-subjects-out style, 8 folds); same forest; AUC of pooled held-out recording scores.
estimand: Faulty: AUC on recordings of subjects who also contributed fitting recordings. Fixed: AUC for recordings of newly recruited subjects.
model_family: Random forest, 50 trees, as in the source's simulation setting (a disease effect, cross-subject and within-subject variability). Chosen by me: the source's simulation fixes 10 features and 100 records per subject; the model is the same family as its real-data classifier.
sizes_note: Source sizes (simulation): 10 features, 100 records per subject, 4 to 32 subjects, half diseased. I use 16 subjects x 60 records x 10 variables = 9.6k values (60 rather than 100 records per subject to keep the check short; rough estimate). The label is held per subject, differing from B2B-10. Source: the record-wise versus subject-wise gap is largest with few subjects and narrows as subjects increase.
exploited_structure: Repeated records of one subject, each carrying the subject's single label, so a subject's records in the fitting data identify the subject's label.

def stat(d):
    x = np.asarray(d["measurements"], dtype=float)
    s, m, v = x.shape
    site_mean = x.mean(axis=1)
    grand = x.mean(axis=(0, 1))
    msb = m * ((site_mean - grand) ** 2).sum(axis=0) / (s - 1)
    msw = ((x - site_mean[:, None, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=(0, 1)) / (s * (m - 1))
    den = msb + (m - 1) * msw
    ok = den > 0
    if not np.any(ok):
        return 0.0
    icc = (msb - msw)[ok] / den[ok]
    return float(np.mean(icc))
